would be decided.

2. Briefly stated the facts as narrated in the FIR by the informant Akbar, father of the minor injured Angoori are that on _____________________________________________________________ MACP No.260/20 ; Angoori Vs. Punit &Anr. Page 1 of 15  21.09.2020, the informant Akbar, who is father of the minor injured, was standing at gate No.1 of Subzi Mandi, Ghazipur,
alongwith cycle filled with vegetables to be sold and at about 11.15 am, his daughter namely Angoori came there for calling him for lunch and at that when she was standing at gate No.1,
one Wagan R Taxi bearing registration No.DL-1RTB-9195, being driven by its driver at a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, came and hit his daughter Angoori.

It is further Angoori vs Punit on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174196212/

sentences.text: It is further stated by him that he caught the driver of the said taxi on the spot, who disclosed his name as Punit and thereafter he took his injured daughter Angoori to LBS Hospital in the offending vehicle, where she had been treated.

The said accident was the subject-matter of investigation of criminal case vide FIR No.0259/20 under section 279/337 of the Indian Penal Code registered at PS PIA.
3.

Both the respondents appeared and filed their replies/
written statements.

3.1. The respondent No.1, in his written statements stated that respondent No.1 is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner as he has not caused any accident at any point of time and respondent No.1 has falsely been implicated in the present matter in collusion with petitioner to extort money.
It is further averred that the offending vehicle was duly insured on the date of accident.

3.2 The respondent No.2 / insurer, in its written statement, conceded that the offending vehicle was i n s u r e d

It contended that the alleged accident did not take place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1, rather it was the petitioner who was negligent on the road and it is a case of contributory negligence on the part of petitioner.
Further, keeping in view of the nature of the injury sustained by the petitioner and assuming some negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle

, respondent No.2 /
insurer offered a sum of Rs.3,50,000/- to the petitioner, as full an final settlement.

4. As per the observations of the Tribunal, since the insurance company had given legal offer, which was not acceptable to the petitioner, apparently the insurance company admitted its liability and issue remains to be decided with respect to quantum of compensation.

Thus, vide order dated 12.02.2023, my learned predecessor framed the following issues:
i). Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?
ii). Relief.

5. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined two witnesses as under:-
(i) PW1 Mohd. Akbar (father of the minor injured) examined himself as eye-witness of the accident and deposed on the strength of his affidavit Ex.PW1/A regarding the manner of accident; grievous injury sustained by his daughter in the accident;

 Copy of Aadhar card of the deponent is Ex.PW1/1  Copy of Aadhar card of minor injured Angoori is

15 pages)  Original bills of the injured are Ex.PW1/4 (colly, 2 pages)
Disability certificate of the minor petitioner is  DAR is Ex.PW1/6 (colly)

(ii) PW2 Dr. Rakesh Malhotra, Associate Professor, Department of Orthopedics, GTB Hospital, Delhi has proved the disability certificate of petitioner Angoori as Ex.
PW2/1 and deposed that the petitioner Angoori suffered permanent locomotor impairment to the tune of 38% of right lower limb.
It was also deposed by him that re-assessment is also recommended after a period of 3 years.
6. On the other hand, respondents opted not to lead any evidence.

7. I have heard the final arguments advanced by Sh. G.S. Bisht and Sh. Pankaj Kumar, learned counsels for petitioner ; Sh. Kurban Ali, Ld. Proxy counsel for R-1 and Sh. Sandeep Singh, Ld.
Counsel for R-2 / insurer and perused the evidence and other materials placed on record.

My findings on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1:-
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 8.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.

As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it s h o u l d  
b e  
p i t t a n c e  
A _____________________________________________________________ man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
9. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on a c c o u n t o f i n j u r y t h e n o r m a l l o n g e v i t y o f t h e ____________________________________________________________

_ person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment,
hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
10. In Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
5 .
 
T h e  
h e a d s  
u n d e r  
w h i c h _____________________________________________________________ compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

Angoori vs Punit on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174196212/
4
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b),
(iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
_____________________________________________________________ 11.

In the light of aforementioned judgments,as accident & rash & negligence driving of R-1 are not disputed, compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses :
12.
Petitioner /PW1 has not filed on record any medical bills of the minor petitioner pertaining to the accident in question.

He has relied on the document Ex.PW1/4 which are the OPD / cash slips of a private hospital at Patna in his name of the year 2018, much prior to the accident and it is inexplicable as to why these payments receipts have been filed on record.

The medical treatment papers of the injured show that she was treated in Government Hospital and it appears that no medical expenses were borne by parents of the minor petitioner due to the injuries sustained in the accident and thus no amount is being granted under this head.

Loss of earning & Loss of studies to the petitioner and her parents during treatment :
13.
The petitioner was merely 08 years old at the time of accident.
Hence, there was no loss of earning to the child victim during treatment.
Further, no loss of earning to the parents of the petitioner is proved on record either.
No loss of study is claimed or proved on record.
Thus, no sum of money is being given under this head.

5

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges :
14.
The petitioner remained under treatment at least till 16.10.2020.

Though no document has been p r o d u c e d  
t o  
s h o w  
t h e _____________________________________________________________ expenses under this head, however, considering the nature of injuries and treatment provided to the petitioner, it may be safely assumed that the minor petitioner must have required the services of an adult person for her care in the hospital and even after her discharge till the time, she was completely recovered.

Further, a reasonable amount must have been spent on the special diet needed for quick recovery after surgery and on transportation facility required for taking injured to hospital for the purpose of treatment.
Thus, a total sum of Rs.30,000/- is granted to petitioner towards conveyance and special diet.

15. Though no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during her treatment, it cannot be ignored that family members of minor petitioner might have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for her routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- as attendant charges.
16. Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.60,000/- (30,000+30,000) under this head.

NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock,hardship, inconvenience and discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in l i f e  
o n  
a c c o u n t  
o f _____________________________________________________________ permanent Disability, loss of marriage prospects :
17.
As per the documents, she initially remained admitted in LBS Hospital post accident for a period of 02 days and thereafter, shifted to AIIMS and remained admitted there from 23.09.2020 to 16.10.2020.
During the course of treatment, she was found to be a case of raw area dorsum of right foot and several operative procedure were conducted during her stay in the hospital.
She underwent 'under LMA and Caudal block, parts painted and rid, wound debired thoroughly, hemostasis secure and loose tagging suturis applied 4th web space and below knee slad application'.
Posteriour sural artery based flat for ankle cover + abdebted digiting minimi flat for 5 th MT cover + K wire fixation of 5th MT of ankle + STSG operative procedures were performed by the doctor.
Minor petitioner remained hospitalized for close to a month.

Aadhar card of the petitioner Ex.PW1/2 shows that the date of birth of minor injured is 15.05.2012 and the accident took place on 21.09.2020, her age was Angoori vs Punit on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174196212/
6 about 08 years on the date of accident.

The minor child was very young and her father is silent in his testimony regarding the status of education of the minor child and does not state anywhere that she was studying at the time of the accident.
Even in DAR, the column regarding education of the victim has been left blank.

As per the disability certificate Ex. PW1/5, she suffers from 38% locomotor impairment in relation to right lower limb and this condition is likely to improve and re-assessment was recommended after a period of 03 years from the date of certificate i.e. 10.09.2022.

The re-assessment time provided is long and file is already ripe and hence final arguments were a d d r e s s e d b y b o t h s i d e s w i t h r e q u e s t f o r p a s s i n g a p p r o p r i a t e __________________________________________________________
___ order on merits.

18. Ld. Counsel for insurance company submitted that under non pecuniary head, a lump sum compensation has to be granted to the petitioner, keeping in mind the guidelines in the judgment Malliakarjun Vs. Divisional Manager.

Ld. Counsel for insurer also submitted that the permanent disability is likely to be less than 38% and the child might also recover completely with time and the re-assessment may show zero percent disability or considerably reduced disability from the temporary disability certificate dated 10.09.2022 and in any case, the permanent disability cannot exceed beyond 38 % and no evidence has been led to reflect that the petitioner has suffered functional disability.

On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for petitioner relied on the citation New India Assurance Company Ltd. Vs. Priyanshu & ors. Decided on 03.01.2018 by Hon'ble Mr. Justice, J.R.
Midha, High Court of Delhi.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Ld. Counsel for the insurance company distinguished the case of the petitioner from the facts of that judgment relied on by the petitioner stating that the said case pertains to exceptional situation where minor suffered from such permanent disability to an extent where accident ruined his life in such a way so as to render his functional disability to be absolute and 100% and further that he was suffering from 76% permanent disability in respect of both lower limbs and his left leg was amputated but in this case, petitioner only suffers from temporary physical disability.
19.

In Civil Appeal No. 7139 of 2013 titled Master Mallikarjun Vs. Division Manager, decided on 26.08.2013, Hon'ble Supreme Court examined the issue regarding the non pecuniary compensation i n  
c a s e  
o f  
c h i l d r e n  
s u f f e r i n g  
f r o m _____________________________________________________________ disability.
As held, the compensation is to be worked out under the non pecuniary heads in addition to the actual amounts incurred for treatment, transportation, assistance of attendant etc.
The main elements of damage in the case of child victim are pain, shock, frustration, deprivation of ordinary pleasure and enjoyment associated with healthy and mobile limbs.
The compensation awarded should enable the child to acquire something or to develop a lifestyle which will offset to some extent the inconvenience or discomfort arising out of the disability.
Appropriate compensation for disability should take care of all the non pecuniary damages.

In other words, apart from this head,
there shall only be the claim for the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, transportation etc.

As further held:
Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard Angoori vs Punit on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174196212/
7 to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various High Courts, we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be , if the disability is above 10 % and upto 30 % to the whole body, Rs. 3 lakhs; upto 60 %, Rs. 4 lakhs; upto 90 %
, Rs. 5 lakhs and above 90 %, it should be Rs. 6 lakhs,

Angoori vs Punit on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174196212/
7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Rs. 1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.

In the case at hand, I am of the considered view that Mallikarjun judgment is squarely applicable and further the judgment relied on by the petitioner pertains to t h e  
c a s e  
o f _____________________________________________________________ amputation, total permanent disability /considerable disability and can be distinguished from the facts and circumstances of this case and no departure from Malliarjun judgment, in my considered view, is warranted.
It is also to be kept in mind that there is physical disability sustained by the minor petitioner, which is likely to improve as per the opinion of the Disability Board.
However, there is nothing brought on record to suggest that the disability is bound to improve to any considerable extent.
The possibility of non improvement cannot be ruled out.

Hence,
a balanced and lenient approach has to be taken by the Tribunal, especially considering that the injured is a minor and a girl child.

20. The judgment above-cited pertain to the year 2013 whereas the accident took place in the year 2020 and inflation increased and further keeping in mind the rate of inflation, the passage of 8 years and the fact that the petitioner is a girl child, I consider it proper to grant lump sum amount of Rs. 5 lakhs to the minor petitioner under this head.
21.

Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-

 1. Medical Expenses Nil  Loss of Earnings Nil  2.
 (during treatment)
 3. Special Diet & Conveyance Rs.30,000/-
 4. Attendant Charges Rs.30,000/-
 5. Pain & Sufferings already Rs.5,00,000/-
 undergone and to be suffered in  future, mental and physical  shock,hardship, inconvenience  and discomforts etc., and loss of _____________________________________________________________ amenities in life on account of permanent Disability, loss of marriage prospects Total Rs.5,60,000/-

8 22. Accordingly, petitioner Baby Angoori is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.5,60,000/-
INTEREST ON AWARD 23.
Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 7.5% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
LIABILITY 24.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured.

Insurance company has not examined any witness to prove the objections raised by them in its written statements or to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured.
In view of above, it is held that respondent no.2/ insurer shall only be entitled to pay the compensation amount in the claim petition.
RELIEF 25.

In view of the aforesaid, this Tribunal awards a compensation of Rs.5,60,000/- (Rupees Five lakhs sixty thousand only) to the petitioner along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of petition till realization to be paid by the respondent no.2 / Bajaj Allianz General Insurance C o m p a n y  
L t d _____________________________________________________________ to the petitioner.
Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.
This award amount is required to be deposited by the insurance company within 30 days.
26. With these observations, the claim petition is disposed of.
27. Files be consigned to Record Room.
